name: CAR-T cell
short_description: One of the patient's own cytotoxic T cells, engineered in the lab to carry a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR): an antibody-derived recognition head on the outside fused to T-cell-receptor activation domains on the inside, letting the cell recognize a chosen surface marker directly, bypassing MHC presentation. Usually made using a lentiviral vector that writes the CAR gene into the patient's own T cells, expanded in the lab and infused back.

sem.1: PASS - measured on a zoomed crop: single round lymphocyte-sized specimen, densely covered in fine ruffled microvilli, matches the cytotoxic-t-cell / real T-cell reference's texture closely; warm amber-gold to violet false colour, deliberately different palette from cytotoxic-t-cell's blue-violet SEM for visual variety (not a scientific claim). By design the CAR is NOT rendered as a distinguishable surface feature -- a single transmembrane receptor protein is several orders of magnitude below SEM resolution, so this style is anatomically honest but cannot show the defining CAR-T feature at all; that is stated plainly here and in verdict decision, not glossed over. Edge-pixel scan confirms fill to all four edges (bg ~20-36/10-29 RGB, no border). No labels per house rule (sem gets none). reference: PASS (2026-08-23) - Wikimedia Commons 'Healthy Human T Cell.jpg', NIAID/NIH, Public Domain: colorized SEM of a single isolated human T lymphocyte, dense ruffled microvillus surface, blue false colour, clean dark background, no baked text/scale bar/border. This is the SAME file already used in the atlas as the reference for cytotoxic-t-cell, reused deliberately and disclosed explicitly (not substituted quietly): a CAR-T cell is a genetically modified but morphologically ordinary cytotoxic T lymphocyte, and its chimeric antigen receptor is a single transmembrane protein a few nanometres across -- far below SEM/light-microscopy resolution, so no micrograph can visually distinguish a CAR-T cell from an unmodified T cell. A search for CAR-T-specific micrographs under a free licence found none. A candidate alternative (NIH/NIAID 'T Regulatory Cells' SEM, Public Domain) was checked and rejected: it is a mixed cluster of T-reg cells with antigen-presenting cells, not a single isolated T lymphocyte, and depicts the wrong T-cell subset.
